subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music For Dramatic Impact Movement And Entertainment
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A Lied is which type of composition?
options: A German art song for voice and piano
questions.explain: The Lied is a German Romantic art song, typically for solo voice and piano.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which progression?
questions.explain: A perfect (authentic) cadence moves from the dominant (V) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: A pivot chord in modulation is best defined as which of the following?
options: The final chord of a phrase only
A chord common to both the old and new keys used to effect the change
A chromatic chord with no diatonic function
A chord borrowed from the parallel major
questions.explain: A pivot chord belongs diatonically to both keys, smoothing the transition during a modulation.

questions.q: In film music, 'underscoring' (or underscore) most accurately means...?
options: A loud climactic fanfare during the titles
Background music supporting a scene's mood or action, typically not heard by the characters
Music that the on-screen characters can hear (diegetic music)
The lyrics printed beneath a song
questions.explain: Underscoring is non-diegetic background music that supports a scene's emotional or dramatic content.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: The continuous sustained background pitch in Indian classical music, often provided by the tanpura, is called the...?
questions.explain: The drone is the sustained pitch (usually tonic and dominant) supplied by the tanpura beneath the melody.

questions.q: Which key signature has four sharps?
questions.explain: E major has four sharps: F sharp, C sharp, G sharp and D sharp.

questions.q: An appoggiatura is best defined as which?
options: A note approached and left by step
A dissonant note approached by leap and resolved by step
questions.explain: An appoggiatura is an accented non-harmony note usually approached by leap and resolved by step.

questions.q: Gamelan music frequently uses 'interlocking' (kotekan) parts, meaning...?
options: All players double the same melody an octave apart
The ensemble plays in strict Western major scales
Two parts combine, each playing alternate notes, to create a single faster composite line
questions.explain: Interlocking parts dovetail, each playing alternate notes so that together they form one rapid composite line.

questions.q: The whole-tone scale, favoured by Debussy, divides the octave into how many equal steps?
questions.explain: The whole-tone scale consists of six pitches a whole tone apart, lacking semitones and a clear tonic.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: The standard twelve-bar blues progression in its basic form follows which sequence of chords (in bars)?
questions.explain: The classic twelve-bar blues uses four bars of I, two of IV returning to I, then V-IV-I across the final four bars.

questions.q: A 'drone' as a textural device (e.g. in Indian or Celtic music) is...?
options: A sustained note or notes held continuously beneath the melody
questions.explain: A drone is a continuously sustained pitch (or pitches) underpinning the melody.

questions.q: The minuet and trio movement of a Classical symphony is typically in which metre?
questions.explain: The minuet, derived from a dance, is in a moderate triple metre.

questions.q: In the typical structure of a North Indian raga performance, the opening section is the 'alap', which is characterised by...?
options: A fast, fixed composition with drumming
A slow, free, unmetred exploration of the raga without tabla
questions.explain: The alap is the slow, unmetred opening that introduces the raga's notes, performed without the tabla.

questions.q: The 'tabla' is...?
options: A pair of hand drums of different sizes and pitches
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of tuned hand drums central to North Indian rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: 'Fusion' music is best defined as...?
options: A style that blends elements of two or more distinct traditions or genres
Music performed only on acoustic instruments
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more traditions or genres, such as jazz-rock or Indian-Western fusion.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: A ritornello in a Baroque concerto is which element?
options: A recurring orchestral refrain returning between solo episodes
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a recurring tutti theme (ritornello) with contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
Speed up the tempo of a track
Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.

questions.q: Handel's 'Messiah' belongs to which genre?
questions.explain: 'Messiah' is an English oratorio, a large sacred work for soloists, chorus and orchestra without staging.

questions.q: In music technology, 'sampling' is best described as...?
options: Recording in a single continuous take
Taking a portion of an existing sound recording and reusing it within a new piece
questions.explain: Sampling reuses a fragment of an existing recording as material within a new track.

questions.q: In jazz harmony, 'comping' refers to...?
options: Compressing the dynamic range in the mix
A pianist or guitarist playing improvised, syncopated chordal accompaniment behind a soloist
Composing a fully notated arrangement in advance
Counting the band in before a number
questions.explain: Comping is the improvised, rhythmic chordal accompaniment provided by piano or guitar behind a soloist.

questions.q: Modal jazz, exemplified by Miles Davis's 'So What', is distinguished from bebop chiefly by its...?
options: Reliance on rapid chord changes every two beats
Use of static modes/scales held over long stretches rather than frequent chord changes
Strict adherence to twelve-bar blues form
questions.explain: Modal jazz bases improvisation on slow-moving modes held for many bars, freeing soloists from rapid chord changes.

questions.q: A melodic sequence is best described as which?
options: The simultaneous sounding of two melodies
The repetition of a melodic pattern at a different pitch level
The inversion of a melodic line
A note held against changing harmony
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic (or harmonic) idea successively higher or lower in pitch.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbol '6' beneath a bass note indicates which chord position?
questions.explain: A bare '6' indicates a first-inversion triad, with the bass note a sixth and a third above it.

questions.q: Wagner's term for a recurring musical theme associated with a character or idea is which?
questions.explain: Wagner used leitmotifs, short recurring themes representing characters, objects or ideas in his music dramas.

questions.q: A circle-of-fifths progression characteristically moves the bass by which interval?
questions.explain: A circle-of-fifths sequence moves root by root down a fifth (equivalently up a fourth) each step.

questions.q: In music production, 'panning' controls...?
options: The overall loudness of the master
The amount of reverb on a track
The placement of a sound within the stereo field (left to right)
questions.explain: Panning positions a sound across the stereo image from left to right.

questions.q: A retardation differs from a suspension in which way?
options: It resolves upward by step rather than downward
questions.explain: A retardation is a suspended note that resolves upward by step, whereas a suspension resolves downward.
